To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the design method is compositional and step-by-step; (ii) the design method allows the designer to focus on the design of each tolerance separately; (iii) the design method uses a simple set of design rules; (iv) the design method can be used to design programs that tolerate multiple faults; and (v) the design method has been used to construct a program that offers a unique tolerance to each class of faults.
(a) the design of multitolerating programs is possible by composing a set of programs, one for each of the fault-classes, and (b) the design can be carried out by a stepwise method.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of programs that are fault-tolerant in the sense that their correctness properties remain intact despite the presence of a variety of failures.
the design of programs that are robust in the face of a variety of fault classes.
the compositional design of multitolerance programs that are correct by construction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our method for the design of multitolerances is based on the following three principles: (i) The design of a multitolerant program is a stepwise procedure, where each step adds one tolerance to the program, and each step can be performed in isolation from the others.
our compositional design method is applicable to any program that is written as a composition of a set of modules, and that each of these modules has been designed to tolerate a specific fault class.

the compositional design method presented in this paper provides an effective means to design programs with potentially unique tolerances to each of the considered failure-classes, and that the method is applicable to a wide variety of fault-tolerance problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show a way to systematically design fault-tolerant programs with multiple tolerances.

we show that the design of a multitolerant program can be reduced to the design of a set of single tolerance programs, each one offering a unique tolerance, that are combined together in a specific manner.
we present a compositional method for designing programs with a potentially unique tolerance for each fault class.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition of two tolerance classes is not a straightforward extension of a single-tolerance design.

the compositional method can be applied to a wide class of fault-tolerant programs and that it is a viable alternative to the more conventional design method of starting with a single-tolerance program and then adding tolerances one-by-one to the program.
compositional and step-wise design of fault-tolerant programs is feasible and can lead to a more efficient design than the design of a program that is tolerant to all faults simultaneously.
